abstract: BACKGROUND: Angiogenesis is essential for tumor growth and metastasis. Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and thymidine phosphorylase (TP)/platelet-derived endothelial cell growth factor (PD-ECGF) are involved in increased angiogenic activity and disease progression in solid tumors. However, there is no information regarding the association of these angiogenic factors with clinicopathologic findings in testicular germ cell tumors (GCTs). METHODS: The authors examined the expression of VEGF and TP as well as microvessel density in GCTs and their association with clinicopathologic findings. Expression of VEGF and TP and microvessel density were examined immunohistochemically in 80 GCTs, including 33 seminomas (25 tumors with organ-confined disease and 8 with metastasis) and 47 nonseminomatous testicular GCTs (NSGCTs) (20 tumors with organ-confined disease and 27 with metastasis). Expression of VEGF also was examined in four GCTs and one nonneoplastic testis by immunoblotting. RESULTS: VEGF protein was expressed more highly in GCTs compared with nonneoplastic testes. VEGF expression in GCTs was correlated significantly with microvessel count (P < 0.001). Both VEGF expression and microvessel count were correlated with metastasis in seminoma (P = 0.008 and P < 0.001, respectively), but only VEGF expression was identified as statistically significant by multiple regression analysis (P = 0.006). Conversely, four variables (VEGF expression, microvessel count, the presence of venous invasion, and the presence of embryonal carcinoma elements in the primary tumor) were correlated with metastasis in NSGCT (P < 0.001, P < 0.001, P = 0.004, and P = 0.029, respectively). However, multiple regression analysis revealed that only VEGF expression and microvessel count were significant factors for metastasis (P < 0.007 and P < 0.001, respectively). In contrast, high levels of TP were observed in infiltrating cells, but not in the majority of cancer cells. CONCLUSIONS: The findings of the current study suggest that VEGF expression is involved in tumor development, angiogenesis, and metastasis in GCT.
abstract_ja:
背景：血管新生は腫瘍の増殖と転移に不可欠である。血管内皮増殖因子(VEGF)とチミジンホスホリラーゼ(TP)/血小板由来内皮細胞増殖因子(PD-ECGF)は、固形腫瘍の血管新生活性と病勢進行に関与する。しかし、精巣胚細胞腫瘍(GCT)におけるこれらの血管新生因子と臨床病理学的所見との関連に関する情報はない。
方法：80例のGCT(セミノーマ33例[臓器限局25例、転移8例]、非セミノーマ性精巣GCT(NSGCT)47例[臓器限局20例、転移27例])において、VEGFおよびTPの発現と微小血管密度を免疫組織化学的に検討し、臨床病理学的所見との関連を調べた。VEGFの発現については、GCT 4例と非腫瘍性精巣1例で免疫ブロットによる検討も行った。
結果：VEGFタンパクはGCTで非腫瘍性精巣に比べ高発現していた。GCTにおけるVEGF発現は微小血管数と有意に相関した(P<0.001)。セミノーマでは、VEGF発現と微小血管数の両者が転移と相関したが(それぞれP=0.008、P<0.001)、重回帰分析で有意だったのはVEGF発現のみだった(P=0.006)。NSGCTでは、VEGF発現、微小血管数、静脈浸潤、原発腫瘍中の胎児性癌成分の存在の4変数が転移と相関した(それぞれP<0.001、P<0.001、P=0.004、P=0.029)。しかし重回帰分析では、転移の有意な因子はVEGF発現と微小血管数のみだった(それぞれP<0.007、P<0.001)。一方、TPは浸潤細胞で高値を示したが、大多数の癌細胞では認められなかった。
結論：本研究の結果は、VEGF発現がGCTの腫瘍発生、血管新生、転移に関与していることを示唆している。
